title: A developer says free, AI-built versions of Adobe's creative apps will soon match the originals.
key_facts: Artcraft debuted seven open-source apps over the weekend that recreate the interface and tools of Adobe's main creative programs.
The apps are written in Rust, with WebAssembly versions for browsers, under MIT and Apache licences.
Developer Brandon Thomas says he used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 to build them as clean-room replacements.
Thomas first said 100% feature parity within a month, then said 99% would take months, not years.
Commenters on Hacker News and elsewhere list many current shortcomings; the apps are in super early alpha.
Thomas plans to fund the apps by selling token-based access to the Artcraft visual AI model.
The article notes that the apps could face legal trouble if their trade dress too closely mimics Adobe's appearance.
quote_evidence: Over the weekend, though, the brand debuted its pivot to a suite of seven open source apps recreating the user interface and tools found in Adobe's Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro.
99% parity will take a while, but I'm sure it'll be measured in months and not years.
why_it_matters_hint: Free replacements for paid creative software would matter to working designers and editors, but the claims are untested.
event_date: 4 Oct 2026 (launch over the weekend of 3 and 4 Oct)
notes: Older news re-dated to 4 Oct 2026. Developer's own claims only.
